narrative:
The 2026 Houston Astros entered the season with a familiar face leading the charge — Carlos Correa, back in an Astros uniform, delivering a clutch early single that set the tone for what Houston hoped would be a return to October glory. The first weeks were a mix of promise and peril, with Bryan King's bullpen blunders costing the team critical games in April, leaving the Astros spinning their wheels as spring turned warm.

May brought another gut punch when Jose Altuve grounded into a season-defining double play, but the resilient Cam Smith answered moments later with a clutch hit that kept Houston alive. June became the Astros' defining month — a stretch where the offense finally roared to life. Joey Loperfido's three-run home run in late June was a thunderclap moment, and Yordan Alvarez's grand slam on the last day of the month capped a remarkable run that pushed Houston above the .500 line and into wild card contention.

The dog days of summer brought a pair of August heroes in Daulton Varsho and Christian Walker, whose back-to-back heroics in a key August 14th game kept the playoff dream breathing. But September delivered cruel blows — Bryan Abreu's inability to contain Ronald Acuña Jr., who launched a grand slam that nearly buried Houston's postseason hopes, and a nervy final stretch that left the Astros clinging to a Wild Card spot by their fingernails.

The Wild Card game against the White Sox proved to be a bridge too far. Reliever Bryan King, a villain throughout the season, was nothing short of catastrophic on the biggest stage — loading the bases and surrendering a pair of runs that put Houston in an early hole they never fully escaped. Nelson Velázquez's two-run shot provided a brief flicker of hope, but Colson Montgomery's solo homer and a Yainer Diaz called third strike to end the game summed up an 81-81 season perfectly: a team with undeniable firepower that too often fell short when it mattered most.
